findings.evidence: WeightTorus.lean:226-230 `conv_lhs => rw [← freeAbelianCharEquiv.symm_apply_apply χ, freeAbelianCharEquiv_symm_apply_ofAdd]` / `rw [torusCharacter_def, Finsupp.prod_fintype _ _ fun _ => zpow_zero _]` / `exact Finset.prod_congr rfl fun j _ => by simp` is the same sequence as SplitTorus/Weight.lean:88-90 `rw [hchar, weightCharacter, freeAbelianCharEquiv_symm_apply_ofAdd, torusCharacter_def, Finsupp.prod_fintype _ _ fun _ => zpow_zero _]` / `exact Finset.prod_congr rfl fun j _ => by simp`.
findings.fix: Add `SplitTorus.apply_weightCharacter (χ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Aˣ) (μ : σ → ℤ) : χ (weightCharacter μ) = torusCharacter (freeAbelianCharEquiv χ) μ` in `SplitTorus/Weight.lean`, reduce `charOfPoint_weightCharacter` to it plus the `hcoord` step, and close the `schemePointsMulEquiv_weightTorus` tail with it.
findings.issue: The tail of the rewritten `schemePointsMulEquiv_weightTorus` (lines 226-230) re-proves, step for step, the character-level fact already proved inside `SplitTorus.charOfPoint_weightCharacter`: `freeAbelianCharEquiv.symm c (ofAdd (equivFunOnFinite.symm μ)) = ∏ j, c j ^ μ j`. findings.fix: Add the general lemma — `(φ : coordinateHopfAlgebra R n ⟶ H) (hφ : I.toIdeal ≤ RingHom.ker φ.hom.toAlgHom.toRingHom) (p) : pointsMulEquiv n ((CommHopfAlgCat.mapPointsFunctor φ).app (CommAlgCat.of R A) p) ∈ hopfIdealPointsSubgroup n I A` — in `HopfIdealPoints.lean` (or its `CommHopfAlgCat`-level form in `HopfIdeal/Points/Naturality.lean`), and derive both `kostantTorusMatrix_mem_toralPoints` and `kostantRootSubgroupMatrix_mem_generatedPoints` from it.
findings.issue: The `hq` block hand-rolls "a point pulled back along a coordinate map that kills the ideal lies in the cut-out subgroup" from `mem_quotientPointsSubgroup_iff` + `RingHom.mem_ker`, while the parallel root-subgroup case (Scheme/Points.lean:103-109) gets the same conclusion from the common-kernel lemma. The general statement is missing from the new `GeneralLinear/HopfIdealPoints.lean` layer the PR introduces for exactly this purpose.

summary: Universe and Finite/Fintype levels are right and the arbitrary-S theorem is correctly the general one, but three general facts are re-proved in special form: the character-level weight evaluation (already inside SplitTorus.charOfPoint_weightCharacter), the definitional split-torus/free-abelian character identity (twice in one proof), and the "point through a coordinate map killing the ideal" membership argument.
